t: Funan is generally considered the first known kingdom in Southeast Asia, though its own name is unknown: 'Funan' is Chinese, and its people may have been Khmer, Austronesian or a mixture of both.

Roman gold medallions of Antoninus Pius and Marcus Aurelius and Persian, Indian and Greek goods found at Óc Eo show a trading state that may have been Ptolemy's Kattigara, where Roman and Chinese merchants met.

Fan Shiman, the 3rd-century 'Great King of Funan', built great ships, attacked more than ten kingdoms and extended his territory five or six thousand li before dying on campaign against Chin-lin, the 'Frontier of Gold'.
dyk: A group of Funanese musicians visited China in 263 CE and so impressed the emperor that he ordered an institute for Funanese music to be founded near Nanking.
ev: By the legend in the Book of Liang, the foreigner Hùntián lands in the Mekong Delta, marries the queen Liǔyè and founds Funan.
The first Funanese embassy reaches Lü Dai, governor of Eastern Wu; a second follows in 243, and the envoys Kang Tai and Zhu Ying sojourn in Funan.
Fan Chan sends embassies to India and China; around 245 the Chinese describe walled villages, palaces, archives and taxes paid in gold, silver, pearls and perfumes.
The Brahmin Qiáochénrú (Kaundinya) is chosen king at Pánpán and changes all the laws to conform to the system of India.
Jayavarman, 'Protégé of Victory', begins a reign that lasts until his death in 514.
Rudravarman kills his brother Gunavarman for the throne and becomes the last known king of Funan, reigning to about 545.
Chenla, Funan's vassal, subjugates the capital T'e-mu and the king migrates south to Nafuna.
Isanavarman of Chenla annexes the territory of Funan at the beginning of the Zhenguan era.

f.capital: Not known; Angkor Borei was perhaps the premier capital, and the Chinese name T'e-mu (Temu), identified by Cœdès with Vyādhapura, then Nafuna
f.founder: Hùntián, identified with the Brahmin Kaundinya, who by legend married the local queen Liǔyè (Somā)
f.predecessor: Settlements of the Mekong Delta inhabited from at least the 4th century BCE
f.successor: Chenla, its former vassal, which annexed Funan's territory in the Zhenguan era (627–649)
